subject: SLO deep-dive: throughput & streaming reproducibility — next steps
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@acmeretail.com>, ops@acmeretail.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-18T15:45:00-08:00
Subject: SLO deep-dive: throughput & streaming reproducibility — next steps

Hi Maria / Acme ops,

Thanks again for carving out time today — good conversation. Quick recap and concrete asks so we can move toward a reproducible qualification run: 

1) High-level goals we captured
   - Tail latency objective: P95 <= 250–300 ms for full-response generation under production workload (you indicated tighter internal goals; please confirm final target).
   - Throughput: sustained peak of ~1.2k concurrent sessions (web user sessions) with expected burst to 2k for 60s windows.
   - Streaming: partial tokens must reach client within ~50–100 ms of generation for the first token and then within target per-token budgets for subsequent tokens.

2) What we attached to kick off the harness
   - acme_prompt_samples_v2.json (seed prompt bundle — annotated with expected response sizes)
   - streaming_load_profile.csv (minute-by-minute traffic shape: baseline, peak, burst)

3) Our recommended initial measurement definitions (we can adjust):
   - Measurement window: 10-minute sustained windows at target concurrency with 5-minute cool-down between windows.
   - Warm-up: 3 minutes of ramp to allow caches to populate when testing with KV-friendly flows.
   - Caching: run both cold-start (no cache) and warm-start (KV cache allowed) passes; we will report both.
   - Streaming metrics: time-to-first-byte (TTFB) for first token, per-token latency percentiles (P50/P95), and end-to-end response completion time.

4) Asks for you (please confirm):
   - Finalized P95 latency target (250 ms? 300 ms?).
   - Confirmation that the attached prompt bundle is representative of production (or a note about gaps).
   - A redacted production trace or sample traffic (headers/sequence lengths only) so we can shape load generator.
   - Whether you prefer Redwood to run the initial harness (we recommend) or grant access to run it yourselves.

Proposed next step: if you approve the above, we schedule Redwood-run qualification on Wed 24 Feb (US time). We’ll deliver a short readout within 48 hours with per-route latency/throughput breakdown and reproducibility notes.

Attachments: [acme_prompt_samples_v2.json (application/json), streaming_load_profile.csv (text/csv)]

Thanks — cc’ing Ben (bench leads) and Grace (CS) to pick up technical and rollout coordination.

—
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0142

From: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@acmeretail.com>

Date: 2027-02-19T09:12:00-05:00
Subject: Re: SLO deep-dive: throughput & streaming reproducibility — next steps

Hi Vanessa / team,

Appreciate the clear recap. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

- Final P95 target: 250 ms for typical web sessions — that’s our internal SLA target for interactive experiences.
- Concurrency: confirmed peak baseline 1,200 concurrent sessions; bursts up to 2,000 for ~1 minute during promotions.
- Streaming: yes, streaming is critical — customers should see partial responses fast. TTFB target ~75 ms, and we care about token-by-token smoothing (not just end-to-end).

We can provide a redacted production trace this afternoon (headers + seq lengths). I’m attaching a small trace sample for your tuning. We would prefer Redwood to run the initial harness so we have an unbiased baseline, but we’ll want a replay artifact and the exact harness config for reproducibility.

Availability: I can do a 30-min follow-up on Mon 22 Feb 10:00–11:30 ET or Wed 24 Feb 09:00–12:00 ET.

Regards,
Maria
Maria Lopez
Head of Platform Engineering, Acme Retail
maria.lopez@acmeretail.com

Attachments: [acme_production_trace_sample.log (text/plain)]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@acmeretail.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-20T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLO deep-dive: throughput & streaming reproducibility — next steps

Maria / Vanessa — thanks for the quick turnaround and the trace. I pulled the sample and sketched a proposed measurement plan and the exact artifacts we’ll need to make the run reproducible. High-level approach below, then a checklist for Acme to confirm.

Measurement methodology (Redwood-run):
- Environment: we will run on a dedicated cluster that mirrors our Dedicated offering: A100x2-equivalent nodes (quantization/profile to be selected after a small model compatibility probe). We will document GPU type, driver, CUDA/cuDNN versions in the readout.
- Model variants: we will test your preferred model family (you specified an Llama-based variant) plus a quantized alternative to measure cost/latency trade-offs.
- Load generation: custom Locust harness with per-session token pacing matched to your trace (we will provide the exact script).
- Warm/cold runs: three cold-start passes (fresh kernel + empty KV cache), three warm-start passes (pre-warmed KV cache and prefix caching allowed). We will report the median/worst across runs, and provide raw logs for reproducibility.
- Streaming metrics:
   * Time-to-first-byte (TTFB_first): from request send to first token arrival (ms)
   * Delta_token_latency: inter-token arrival times (median/P95)
   * Completion latency: last token arrival (P50/P95/P99)
- Observability: token-level traces, per-request kernel selection logs, and per-gpu utilization samples will be captured.

Reproducibility checklist (items we need from Acme):
1) Redacted production trace (we have the sample — thank you). Full trace preferred: timestamps, seq lengths, and the fraction of streaming vs batch requests.
2) Confirmation of model checkpoint(s) + tokenizer spec (repo or artifact URL).
3) Any per-request pre/post-processing that happens client-side (e.g., truncation, prompt templating) documented.
4) Network characteristics: typical RTT from your user base to our region (or the CDN region we should emulate).
5) Bench windows you prefer us to highlight (e.g., 09:00–10:00 PT daily promotion spike).

Deliverables and artifacts we will publish after the run:
- Raw logs and the Locust config used (so you can re-run).
- A reproducibility package: Dockerfile + scripts + seed prompt bundle (acme_prompt_samples_v2.json) + run instructions.
- Per-route and per-model latency/throughput CSVs and a short findings deck.

Estimated timeline if you approve:
- Tuesday (tomorrow): we finalize model checkpoint and confirm GPU profile.
- Wed 24 Feb: Redwood-run qualification (morning PT).
- Fri 26 Feb: readout and reproducibility package delivery.

Attachments: [streaming_load_profile.csv]  

Action items for you (Maria): please confirm P95=250ms, share full trace and model checkpoint by Tue EOD PT, and confirm whether we should include your in-house quantized variant.

—
Ben Carter
Bench Lead, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>

Maria — thanks, that all sounds good. Confirming items and next steps: 

- Confirmed P95 target: 250 ms (we’ll treat 250 as the primary target and include 300 as a contingency SLO).
- Redwood will run the initial harness on Wed 24 Feb (start 09:00 PT). Ben will lead the run; Grace will handle CS coordination and success criteria.
- Please share: full redacted trace, model checkpoint link, and any pre/post-processing docs by Tue 23 Feb 17:00 PT. If sharing via Drive, drop the folder link into the HubSpot deal record (linked above).
- We’ll provide the Locust script + Dockerfile up front so you can review the harness prior to the run; after the run we’ll give you the full reproducibility package.

If any change to timing, reply here and we’ll re-align. Otherwise we’ll see you remotely on Wed morning and deliver the readout by Fri.

Thanks — cc’ing Grace for scheduling and run ops.
